    Quick and easy pistachio frosting recipe, homemade with simple ingredients. This green buttercream icing is smooth, rich, creamy and packed with real pistachio butter (spread or paste). Great for piping swirls on cupcakes as well as cake decorating.

    One of my favorite nuts ever to snack on, or to use in cake decorating and even baking are pistachios. Today's recipe takes my love of this mighty nut to a whole new level! if you and your family is like me as well, then you should also check out my Pistachio Cake (With Cake Mix) and this Condensed Milk Fudge (Cranberry and Pistachio).

    Key ingredients

    • Butter- This should be unsalted and at room temperature.
    • Pistachio butter- You can also use pistachio paste or spread. Just make sure it looks green in color and not brownish.
    • Powdered sugar- Make sure it's sifted to remove all lumps.
    • Extracts and oils- I like to use a combination of vanilla and pistachio flavors. Try to use clear extracts or oils, if you can.
    • Salt- This helps to cut the sweetness.
    • Food coloring- Use green gel food coloring to enhance the color of the icing.

    Variations

    • Mix in other extracts- Such as almond or maple for an additional layer of flavor.
    • Use this as a filling in cupcakes- Check out this post for more details: How to Make Filled Cupcakes (Stuffed Cupcakes).
    • Use this for piping cupcakes- Check out this post for information: How to Decorate Cupcakes (Pipe). It also pairs wonderfully with my Almond Cupcakes (Sour Cream Cupcakes).
    • Use it to decorate a cake- It is ideal to use in my favorite Chocolate Cake and Vanilla Cake (From Scratch).
    • Use it for decorating cookies- Pair it with Cut Out Sugar Cookies (With Cake Mix) or Pistachio Cookies (Cut Out).
    • Make this with butter shortening combo- This will add more stability. Just replace half the unsalted butter with shortening.

    How to make easy pistachio frosting recipe from scratch?

    1. Whip butter and pistachio butter- Until light and fluffy.
    2. Add salt and extracts- Mix until combined.
    3. And powdered sugar- Do this gradually.
    4. Mix in milk- Do this gradually too until you have a smooth mixture.
    5. Add food coloring- To brighten the green color.

    Tips and techniques

    • Use green colored pistachio spread, butter or paste- There are many in the marketplace that have a brownish green hue. If you use that, your icing will be more earthy and pale brown in color than green.
    • Use green gel food coloring- To enhance the green shade, per your preference.
    • Don't use liquid food coloring- Because it can thin out the icing. Use edible gel colors.
    • Different brands of butters and spreads have different consistencies- Some are thick and chunky. Some are smooth and creamy. As a result, you may need to adjust the amount of powdered sugar and milk to get the consistency you desire.
    • If icing is too thin- Mix in more powdered sugar.
    • If icing is too thick- Mix in more milk. 
    • Please use clear extracts and oils- To prevent adding a brownish hue to the icing.
    • Use sifted powdered sugar- To remove any lumps. This ensures the smoothest consistency.
    • Use unsalted butter- To prevent this icing from becoming too salty.
    • Is this icing enough? It's enough to frost 24 cupcakes (depending on the design) and one 8x2 round cake.

    Recipe FAQs

    Why is my frosting brown?

    This can be a result of using a spread that was made from toasted or roasted pistachios, which have a light brown color. Also, butter has a natural yellow tinge and extracts have a brown tinge and when those mix with the greenish brown hues of the nut butter, you will end up with a dull brown or khaki shade. Most importantly, the natural raw color of pistachio paste is not bright green. It's actually a pale olive tan color.

    Why is my icing gritty?

    There can be a few reasons: 1)It was not mixed properly and the powdered sugar hasn't incorporated into the butter completely. 2)Your powdered sugar was not sifted and had little lumps, resulting in a chunky texture. 3) You did not use enough liquid (milk) to combine the ingredients smoothly.

    What is pistachio spread, pistachio butter and pistachio paste?

    They are all made with ground pistachios. However, pistachio spread is usually sweetened with sugar. It can also have other ingredients like oil, extracts, flavorings and even color. It has a much smoother consistency, similar to Nutella and Biscoff. On the other hand, pistachio paste and pistachio butter are made from with 100% ground pistachios and nothing else. They are also darker in color and have a slightly chunky texture.

    Why is my icing soft and runny? How to fix this?

    There could be a few reasons for this: 1)Too much liquid was added or 2)Not enough powdered sugar was added. To fix this, mix in more powdered sugar until you achieve the desired consistency.

    Storage

    • Refrigerate- In a sealed container for up to 1 week.
    • Freeze- In a sealed container for up to 1 month. When you are ready to enjoy it, thaw and then whip again to make it fluffy again.
    • Room temperature- This can stay out for 3-5 hours away from direct heat, sunlight and moisture.
    • Make ahead- This can easily be made 1 day in advance and stored in fridge.

    Recipe

    Easy Pistachio Frosting (Buttercream Icing)

    Abeer Rizvi
    Quick and easy pistachio frosting recipe, homemade with simple ingredients. This green buttercream icing is smooth, rich, creamy and packed with real pistachio butter (spread or paste). Great for piping swirls on cupcakes as well as cake decorating.
    No ratings yet
    Print Recipe Pin Recipe
    Prep Time 10 minutes mins
    Total Time 10 minutes mins
    Course Dessert

    Calories 1016 kcal

    Ingredients
      

    • 1 cup Butter Unsalted, Room temperature
    • ⅓ cup Pistachio butter Can also use pistachio spread or pistachio paste. Just make sure to get something that looks green and not pale brown.
    • ¼ teaspoon Salt
    • 1 teaspoon Vanilla extract Try to use clear extract so that it doesn't tint the icing.
    • ½ teaspoon Pistachio extract or oil Optional. I like to use pistachio oil because it has a stronger aroma and it's clear and doesn't tint the icing.
    • 3-5 cups Powdered sugar Sifted. Start with 3 cups. Add more if necessary after you add milk, to get the consistency you desire.
    • 1-3 tablespoon Milk Or heavy cream. Start with 1 tablespoon and add more as necessary to get the consistency you desire.
    • Few drops Green gel food coloring

    Instructions
     

    • In a mixing bowl, whip unsalted butter and pistachio butter until you have a light and fluffy mixture.
    • Add salt, clear vanilla extract, pistachio extract (if using) and mix until combined.
    • Add powdered sugar (½ cup at a time), while continuing to mix until you have added 3 cups.
    • Add milk (1 tablespoon at a time), while continuing to mix until you reach the desired consistency. 
    • If you feel like your icing is too soft and thin, mix in more powdered sugar now.
    • If you feel like it's too thick, mix in more milk.
    • Add green gel food coloring and mix until color is evenly distributed. Enjoy.

    Notes

    • Since the consistencies of pistachio butters vary so much in the marketplace, you may need to add more powdered sugar or milk. This is why I recommend starting with 3 cups of powdered sugar and 1 tablespoon milk and adding more as necessary until you have a piping consistency. 
    • Please use clear extracts and oils to prevent adding a brownish hue to the icing.
    • You can use any of these in this recipe: pistachio butter, spread or paste.
    • Please make sure whatever pistachio butter you are buying is already green in color and not earthy brownish green.
    • You can enjoy the icing as is but to enhance the green shade of the icing, mix in a few drops of green gel food coloring at the end. This will not affect the flavor at all. It will just make the appearance nicer and brighter.
    • Use sifted powdered sugar to remove any lumps. This ensures you have the smoothest icing consistency.
    • This icing is enough to frost 24 cupcakes (depending on the design) and one 8x2 round cake.
    • Read additional tips and variations above.
    • Leftovers can be stored in a sealed container for up to 1 week.
